correctness.rationale: Rotation weights leave just z and z² conjugate(z) in degree at most three. In a radial–tangential frame the real derivative columns, up to common rotation, are a+3bs and i(a+bs); their determinant is m+4cs+3ds². Minimizing on s≥0 gives precisely the strict inequality in the Finding, including singularity at equality. It is sufficient since the squared-radius image H(s)=s|a+bs|² runs strictly increasingly from zero to infinity and each angular map is a rotation; the local smooth inverses then give the global smooth inverse. The fixed-radius quadratic has roots of opposite signs; H(s)−s determines strict monotonic radial motion on either side, and at the positive root H′ is also the multiplier in ordinary radial distance. The two constructions have |a|<1, s*=1, Q(1)=2 and the specified circle rotation. A commuting real-linear map must commute with the nonreal linear part and so is a complex scalar; the cubic term forces unit modulus. No degree-two equivariant term exists. The verification note and checker were inspected, not executed; the exact identities and boundary checks follow from the displayed proof and arithmetic.

value.rationale: This is a classification across the entire first nonlinear rotational polynomial class, not a selected numerical example. It locates the singular global-inverse boundary, the entire basin boundary and rotation dynamics, and gives minimal-degree counterexamples to inferring global attraction from a unique local sink, even for a smooth global inverse and exact continuous rotational symmetry.
